question: Is the recorded MODULE.bazel.lock input digest the SHA-256 of the on-disk bytes, in every lock family, for LF and CRLF files?
verdict: CONFIRMED under the default digest function on every version run; REFUTED under a non-default --digest_function startup option
extension: //:ext.bzl%x4 (root module, not reproducible, module_ctx.read(label) per file)

workspace.inputs: inputs/<path> goes to <path> (the workspace root holds lf.lock, sub/pkg/nested.lock, ...)
workspace.bazel_6: 6.6.0 also needs an empty WORKSPACE file at the root and --enable_bzlmod on every command
workspace.command: `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` in that workspace writes the MODULE.bazel.lock committed as locks/<bazel>.MODULE.bazel.lock

key_rules.accumulatedFileDigests: key is '@@' + label, colon kept ('@@//sub/pkg:deep/dir/file.lock'); a space is written as is
key_rules.recordedFileInputs: key is '@@//' + workspace-relative path; a space is written as is
key_rules.recordedInputs: list of strings 'FILE:' + escaped('@@//' + path) + ' ' + value; the escape writes backslash as two backslashes, newline as backslash n, space as backslash s

other_digests_of_lf_lock.note: the sha1 cells recorded exactly this value; the blake3 value is in digest_function[]

digest_function_note: digest_function[] rows with a lock_file have the lock Bazel wrote under that startup option, byte for byte; the others have rows only. A sha1 value is 40 hex digits. A blake3 value is 64, the length of a SHA-256, so length cannot tell the two apart: the SHA-256 comparison fails for every input, the empty file included. The option is set on the command line or by a `startup` line in an rc file; the lock does not name it

inputs.label: //:crlf.lock
inputs.what: CRLF line endings (lf.lock with every LF made CRLF)

inputs.label: //sub/pkg:deep/dir/file.lock
inputs.what: file in a subdirectory of a package
